# Flying Star Aviator Private Limited
> DGCA-approved Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) and ATPL ground-class training institute in Dwarka, New Delhi, India. Operating since 2008, Flying Star Aviator prepares aspiring pilots for DGCA examinations and airline careers, and also provides B2B aviation services (aircraft management, MRO, CAMO, charter).

## Pilot training & courses
- [CPL Ground Classes](https://www.flystar.co.in/courses/cpl): DGCA Commercial Pilot Licence ground training — Air Navigation, Meteorology, Air Regulations, Technical General.
- [ATPL Ground Training](https://www.flystar.co.in/courses/atpl): Airline Transport Pilot Licence ground classes for airline career advancement.
- [Airline Preparation](https://www.flystar.co.in/courses/airline-preparation): Airline interview and assessment preparation.
- [Pilot Training Overview](https://www.flystar.co.in/pilot-training): Training pathways in India, USA, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa.
- [How to Become a Pilot](https://www.flystar.co.in/become-a-pilot/become-pilot): Step-by-step guide to becoming a commercial pilot in India after Class 12.
- [PPL Training in India](https://www.flystar.co.in/pilot-training/ppl): Private Pilot Licence eligibility — a Class Ten pass, not 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics; Composite Paper and Aircraft & Engine subjects; 70% pass mark; passed papers valid two and a half years.
- [CPL Flight Training in India](https://www.flystar.co.in/pilot-training/cpl): How ground training and flying training divide between a ground school and a DGCA-approved Flying Training Organisation, the 200-hour minimum, and DGCA theory requirements.
- [Converting a Foreign Licence to a DGCA Licence](https://www.flystar.co.in/pilot-training/guide-to-conversion): DGCA conversion under CAR Section 7, Series G, Part I — the 10-hours-PIC-in-24-months currency rule, Indian written examinations and a skill test with a DGCA-approved examiner.
- [Pilot Training in the Maldives](https://www.flystar.co.in/pilot-training/maldives): Verifying a school against the Maldives Civil Aviation Authority's published list of approved flight training organisations, and what DGCA conversion then requires.
- [Pilot Training in Sri Lanka](https://www.flystar.co.in/pilot-training/sri-lanka): CAASL Commercial Pilot Licence requirements — minimum age 18, Class I medical, English Language Proficiency at ELPC Level 4 or higher — and the route back to an Indian licence.

## DGCA guides
- [DGCA Full Form & Role](https://www.flystar.co.in/dgca/full-form): What DGCA (Directorate General of Civil Aviation) is and what it regulates.
- [DGCA Medical Requirements](https://www.flystar.co.in/dgca/medical): Class 1 and Class 2 medical requirements for pilots in India.
- [DGCA Ground Classes](https://www.flystar.co.in/dgca/ground-classes): CPL & ATPL ground classes in Dwarka, Delhi.
- [DGCA Computer Number](https://www.flystar.co.in/dgca/computer-number): Eligibility (10+2 with Physics and Mathematics; PPL category excepted), no maximum age limit, lifetime validity, one number per candidate, Board Verification Certificate mandatory for new candidates, PDF-only documents, and the hard copy that must be posted to the Central Examination Organization, R.K. Puram, New Delhi 110066.
- [RTR(A) Training](https://www.flystar.co.in/rtr): Radio Telephony Restricted (Aeronautical) exam preparation.

- [DGCA Ground Classes vs Self-Study](https://www.flystar.co.in/blog/dgca-ground-classes-vs-self-study): DGCA does not require ground-class attendance to sit the CPL theory papers — CAR Section 7, Series B, Part I asks only for a computer number and 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics. Covers the Rs 2,500-per-paper examination fee, the 70% pass mark, five-year paper validity, and which route suits which candidate.

- [DGCA Exam Fees](https://www.flystar.co.in/blog/dgca-exam-fees): DGCA states Rs 2,500 per paper for Flight Crew Licence online examination, not refundable under any circumstances, and publishes no separate fee for the Online On-Demand Examination route.
- [DGCA OLODE vs Regular Sessions](https://www.flystar.co.in/blog/dgca-olode-vs-regular-exams): What the on-demand examination route changes and what it does not — eligibility, syllabus, pass mark and paper validity are identical to a scheduled session.
- [Common Misconceptions About DGCA Exams](https://www.flystar.co.in/blog/dgca-exam-misconceptions): Chemistry is not required, there is no maximum age, ground classes are not mandatory, and a PPL needs only a Class Ten pass — each checked against DGCA's published rules.
- [DGCA Board Verification Certificate](https://www.flystar.co.in/blog/dgca-board-verification-certificate): A certificate from your board confirming a mark sheet is authentic, mandatory for all NEW Flight Crew candidates before registration.
- [ATPL Eligibility in India](https://www.flystar.co.in/blog/atpl-eligibility-india): An ATPL applicant should already hold an Indian CPL, defence personnel may qualify on 500 hours including 200 as Pilot-in-Command, and an ATPL is not issued on a single-engine aircraft.

## Key facts
- A DGCA Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) in India requires a minimum of 200 hours of flight time, a Class 1 medical, and passes in DGCA theory subjects (Air Navigation, Meteorology, Air Regulations, Technical General) plus the RTR(A) licence.
- Minimum age for a CPL is 18; candidates need Class 12 with Physics and Mathematics.
- A DGCA Class 1 medical is mandatory for a CPL; a Class 2 medical is the minimum to begin flying training.
- Flying Star Aviator has provided DGCA CPL/ATPL ground classes in Dwarka, Delhi since 2008.
- Flying Star Aviator Private Limited operates a single training centre, in Dwarka, New Delhi. It is a ground-training institute and does not own a flying school; flying hours are logged at partner DGCA-approved Flying Training Organisations.
- DGCA ground classes are NOT mandatory to appear for DGCA theory examinations. Per DGCA CAR Section 7, Series B, Part I, a CPL candidate needs a computer number issued by the Central Examination Organisation and a 10+2 pass with Physics and Mathematics. Ground school attendance is not a listed eligibility condition.
- The pass mark for each DGCA theory paper is 70%. There is no aggregate across papers.
- A cleared CPL or ATPL theory paper remains valid for five years. A cleared PPL paper is valid for two and a half years.
- DGCA theory subjects differ by licence. PPL: a Composite Paper plus Aircraft & Engine / Instruments in general and specific. CPL: Air Navigation, Aviation Meteorology, Air Regulation, and Aircraft & Engine / Instruments in general, specific and performance. ATPL adds Radio Aids and Instruments plus an oral examination, with 70% required in the oral as well.
- An ATPL applicant should already hold an Indian Commercial Pilot Licence. Defence personnel may instead qualify on 500 hours of flying experience including 200 as Pilot-in-Command. An ATPL is not issued on a single-engine aircraft.
- A Board Verification Certificate, issued by the candidate's board to confirm a mark sheet is authentic, is mandatory for all NEW DGCA Flight Crew candidates before registration. Candidates allotted a computer number before the Pariksha portal launched do not need one.
- To appear in DGCA PPL theory examinations a candidate needs a computer number and a pass in Class Ten or equivalent. The 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics requirement applies to the Commercial Pilot Licence, not the PPL. (DGCA CAR Section 7, Series B, Part I.)
- DGCA ATPL theory eligibility requires the applicant to already hold an Indian Commercial Pilot Licence. An ATPL is not issued on a single-engine aircraft.
- To convert a foreign pilot licence to an Indian one, DGCA requires the rating on the foreign licence to be current — at least 10 hours as Pilot-in-Command in the twenty-four months preceding the application — plus written examinations through the Central Examination Organisation and a skill test with a DGCA-approved examiner in India. (DGCA CAR Section 7, Series G, Part I, Issue II, Revision 4, 9 September 2019.)
- The DGCA Flight Crew Licence examination fee is Rs 2,500 per paper, and it is not refundable under any circumstances. DGCA publishes no separate fee for the Online On-Demand Examination (OLODE) route; a Rs 5,000 OLODE figure is widely repeated online but has no primary source. (DGCA Pariksha Flight Crew FAQ, questions 13 and 14.)
- A DGCA Computer Number is the unique lifetime identifier allotted to a Flight Crew candidate by the Central Examination Organization, Office of the DGCA. It is required to apply for any DGCA pilot examination, a candidate may hold only one, and it covers every Flight Crew examination category.
- There is no maximum age limit to register as a DGCA Flight Crew candidate. Except for the PPL category, applicants need 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics — not Chemistry.
- A DGCA Computer Number is not generated automatically on submission. For new candidates it is allotted only after DGCA scrutinises the online application against a hard copy posted to the CEO, DGCA, East Block-III, Level-III, R.K. Puram, New Delhi 110066.
